definition: In the history of philosophy and psychology, res extensa refers to extended material reality: the outer world of bodily, mechanically moving things. In Descartes’ dualism, it is contrasted with res cogitans, the thinking mind.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Dualism (in philosophy); pinned source text

reasons: “Bodily” is not supported by the packet; the source only describes res extensa as the “outer world of extended mechanically moving things” and contrasts it with res cogitans.
The definition slightly modernizes and generalizes the historical description; it should stay closer to the Descartes-specific wording in the source.

The packet supports the contrast between “the inner world of consciousness” and “the outer world of extended mechanically moving things,” but it does not explicitly describe res extensa as “bodily” (the definition adds “bodily” beyond the packet).

The packet discusses this as part of “Modern philosophy” and Descartes’s dualism; it does not support framing the term as belonging to “philosophy and psychology” specifically (the definition adds “psychology” not evidenced in the packet excerpt).
